prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. One finished landscape 3:2 full-bleed picture-book illustration, one coherent scene and moment, no panels or contact sheet. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
 No named child cast: Kit and Zoe MUST NOT appear. Include unnamed human workers/adults ONLY when explicitly required by this particular scene; otherwise show only the natural subjects. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Ready for Wings; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: One illustrative two-striped grasshopper, Melanoplus bivittatus, across its egg, nymph and adult stages in a grassy field. Six legs, large rear jumping legs, two antennae, brown-green body with two pale lengthwise stripes; no butterfly chrysalis or caterpillar body.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): Soil egg pod shown in a natural cutaway; One focal young grasshopper and its successive stages, never duplicate individuals in one scene; Grass blades with feeding notches; Empty shed outer skins distinct from live animals
 Input references lock identity, prop design and location; compose a NEW image for the exact scene, never reproduce the reference-board layout. The reference and overall prop list may contain finished objects and later story events: these are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY, not permission to show them now. Show only the people, objects and development stage required below.
Page 8. Printed prose (NOT text to put in art): The little hopper grows wings in stages.
Now it can hop and fly.
Required illustration: The same adult rests with long wings folded along its striped body on the opening grass blade; an old small feeding notch remains nearby. Continuity: Ending identifies the winged adult as the result of the earlier egg and nymph stages; no claim every grasshopper species is winged.
Exact current state: Ending identifies the winged adult as the result of the earlier egg and nymph stages; no claim every grasshopper species is winged.
Do not add later events, duplicate props or a separate inset. No written title; the app renders live text.
CURRENT SCENE INVENTORY: ONE ADULT rests on a grass blade with long narrow forewings folded naturally covering hind wings along striped body; six legs, two antennae. Small earlier feeding notch beside mouth on same blade persists; no feeding action required. No old skin, eggs, second insect or cutaway. Keep animal above central curved blade with physical grips.
Single continuous scene, no diagram or duplicate poses from reference. Landscape3:2 1536x1024. Compose animal and any old skin in central70% width and central74% height; all antenna/leg/wing tips at least12% from every edge. Natural coherent scale and support, clean flat 2D bold outlines, no grain or paint texture. Reference studies indicate design only; use only correct stage and objects specified now.
